title: Ransomware Riptide
subtitle: Ransomware at City Hall and the Island Decision

brief.userPrompt: Ransomware detonates on the business network at City Hall on a Monday morning: the billing system MBW-CIS-01, the AMI head-end MBW-AMI-01 and the file server MBW-FS-01 are encrypted and a ransom note names the city. The SCADA domain MBWSCADA trusts the business domain and firewall rule FW-R-17 carries SMB from the engineering workstation to the backup server MBW-BKP-01, so City IT wants to island the control network while the plant decides whether to go to manual operations, customer service loses billing and the outage map, and the mayor asks whether the water is safe.
constraints: Every email address of the City and the department uses the exercise domain millbrook-oh.example; outside parties use fictional domains and the fictional outlets of the communications plan (Channel 4, the Millbrook Courier); never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; outside parties (City IT's vendors, the FBI, CISA, Ohio EPA DDAGW, the Carver County Health Commissioner, the media) are played by the SimCell, not seated as players.

overview.theme: Business-network ransomware, the paths into the control network, and running the plant without the City’s systems
overview.threat: Ransomware detonates on the City of Millbrook business network (the MILLBROOK domain) on a Monday morning and encrypts the billing system MBW-CIS-01, the AMI head-end MBW-AMI-01 and the file server MBW-FS-01 through the backup service account. The same account reaches toward the control network along the two paths the OT plan already lists as finding F-5: the nightly SMB rule FW-R-17 between MBW-EWS-01 and the backup server MBW-BKP-01, and the MBWSCADA → MILLBROOK domain trust on FW-R-14. A payload is staged on the hot-standby SCADA server MBW-SCADA-SRV02 to run at noon. MBW-BKP-01, which holds every recovery copy the City has, is encrypted too.
overview.operationalImpact: Customer Service loses billing, the customer portal and the outage map; the lab loses LIMS; the PIO loses the file server and may lose the MillbrookAlert console. The plant itself keeps running in automatic, but the SCADA / IT Security Manager must decide within 30 minutes whether to island the control network (OT Plan 10.3), and the Incident Commander must decide whether the plant stays in automatic with an operator watching MBW-HMI-01 or goes to manual operations with two operators per shift (ERP 7.5.1, OT Plan 8). The Mayor, the media and a dialysis center ask whether the water is safe; the answer has to come from grab samples, not from the absence of alarms. Recovery takes days: the SCADA servers are rebuilt from clean media, the PLC-02 flow-pacing logic exists only in the PLC and on the integrator’s laptop (finding F-2), and the City does not pay.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Within 15 minutes of the first report, move DWS coordination to phone and radio DWS-1 (ERP Section 5: assume the City email tenant and MBW-FS-01 are read by the intruder) and keep the Control Room, Customer Service and the PIO on one set of facts.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Decide within 30 minutes of the SIEM alert whether to island the control network (OT Plan 10.3), and decide on the evidence whether the plant stays in automatic with an operator watching MBW-HMI-01 or moves to manual operations (ERP 7.5.1), with the staffing that requires.

objectives.name: Technical Analysis
objectives.text: Find and close the paths from the MILLBROOK domain into the control network (FW-R-17, FW-R-14 and the MBWSCADA trust) without powering off or reimaging the affected hosts (OT Plan 10.7), and establish which recovery copies survive.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Run the OT Plan 10.5 ransomware checklist, the Section 12 reporting clocks (CISA, FBI, Ohio EPA DDAGW, WaterISAC, the insurance carrier) and the Customer Service workarounds, and answer “is the water safe?” from sample results.

roles.name: Director of Water Operations (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Manages the water treatment and distribution system, including the decision to declare a Level 3 emergency and to initiate manual operations.
standingOrders: Trust the field: if the screen and the field disagree, act on the field reading and the grab sample.
Coordinate by phone and radio DWS-1 during a cyber incident; email and MBW-FS-01 may be read by the intruder (ERP Section 5).
Approve islanding the control network when OT Plan 10.3 is invoked; record every decision on ERP-1.
Manual operations need two operators per shift; plan relief and OHWARN before you need them.

roles.name: SCADA / IT Security Manager (Technical Lead)
roles.description: Owns the control network, its firewall rules and remote access, the islanding decision and the technical investigation; works with City IT, which owns the business network.
standingOrders: Evidence first: do not power off, reimage or “clean” the SCADA servers, HMIs or MBW-EWS-01 (OT Plan 10.7).
On business-network ransomware, have FW-R-17, FW-R-22 and FW-R-14 disabled at once; do not wait for the islanding decision (OT Plan 10.5).
Decide within 30 minutes whether to island the control network and tell the Incident Commander why.
Make the CISA report within 24 hours, immediately if equipment was operated without authorization (OT Plan 12).

roles.name: Public Information Officer (PIO)
roles.description: Owns customer notices, boil-water advisories, social media, and the press.
standingOrders: Use the cyber holding statement (PCP Section 10.5) until the Director and the Water Quality Manager approve more.
Never confirm a ransom demand or talk about payment: “the City is working with law enforcement and will not discuss that.”
Say what is being tested and when the next update comes; never say “no contamination” without a result.
Log every media call and rumor; the Deputy PIO answers posts with the approved lines (PCP Section 8).

roles.name: Water Quality Manager (Compliance)
roles.description: Owns sampling, the lab, regulatory reporting, and public-notice triggers.
standingOrders: Answer water-quality questions from grab samples, not from the absence of alarms.
When LIMS is down, record results on the paper bench sheets; compliance reports to DDAGW are still due on their dates.
Notify Ohio EPA DDAGW within 24 hours of a cyber event that affects the ability to monitor water quality (OT Plan 12).
An advisory needs a trigger in ERP Section 9; a rumor is not one.

roles.name: Customer Service Lead (Customer Service)
roles.description: Owns the customer service center, the surge phone line, the printed critical-customer list and the manual intake and billing workarounds while MBW-CIS-01, the portal and the outage map are down.
standingOrders: Paper first: when MBW-CIS-01 or the portal fails, switch to the paper intake form and the printed critical-customer list (OT Plan 10.5).
No disconnections for non-payment while billing is down.
Log complaint patterns to the Control Room; a cluster of taste, odor or pressure calls is a detection input (ERP Section 6).
Critical customers hear from DWS before the public does (PCP Section 6).

phases.title: Encrypted at City Hall
phases.goal: Recognize a business-network ransomware event, move coordination off City systems and start the OT Plan 10.5 checklist before the plant is touched.
beats: At 09:07 the Distribution Office reports on radio DWS-1 that its files are renamed and a ransom note is on every desktop; Customer Service sees the same on MBW-CIS-01.
At 09:12 the City SIEM shows the backup service account encrypting MBW-FS-01 and MBW-CIS-01 and logging on to MBW-EWS-01 in the control network.
At 09:15 City IT asks whether anything on the plant side depends on the MILLBROOK domain before it resets the domain.
At 09:22 the Millbrook Courier asks whether the City has been hacked and whether the water plant is affected.
At 09:30 a four-minute dip on chlorine analyzer AIT-301 looks like an attack on the plant; it is the Monday calibration.

phases.title: The Island Decision
phases.goal: Decide whether to island the control network and whether the plant can stay in automatic, as evidence of spread toward the control network arrives.
beats: At 10:05 the Control Room reports a command window flashing on MBW-EWS-01 and the AquaSight designer failing to start.
At 10:08 the response firm finds SMB back to MBW-EWS-01 on FW-R-17 and two MILLBROOK logons to MBW-SCADA-SRV02 through the trust.
At 10:15 Channel 4 asks about a ransom note that says “we control your water”; at 10:25 the Mayor wants a yes or no on water safety.
At 10:30 the Plant Superintendent sets out what manual operations will cost in operators, sampling and days.

phases.title: Manual Mode
phases.goal: Run the plant without the City’s systems and decide how recovery will be done, with a payload staged on a SCADA server and the backups gone.
beats: At 11:05 a scheduled task is found on MBW-SCADA-SRV02, set to run a new service at 12:00.
At 11:10 City IT relays the actor’s offer and the backup picture and asks for DWS’s recommendation by 11:30: the decision point.
At 11:25 Carver Kidney Center asks whether to stop dialysis; at 11:30 a viral post says hackers added chemicals to the water.
At 11:35 the Chemical Building door is found to accept a revoked contractor badge from the cached PACS list.

phases.title: Rebuild and Report
phases.goal: Confirm water quality, make the reports, hold the line with the media and Customer Service, and plan a rebuild that will take days.
beats: At 12:05 the noon payload runs on MBW-SCADA-SRV02; whether it reaches anything else depends on what the players isolated.
At 12:10 the lab reports normal noon grab samples on paper bench sheets.
At 12:15 the Courier hears the City is negotiating and that card numbers are on the dark web; at 12:25 Customer Service is buried in calls.
At 12:30 the integrator offers to come on site with the laptop that holds the only other copy of the PLC-02 logic.

msel.event: STARTEX: It is 09:00 on Monday, October 26. Demand is normal at about 9 MGD and the plant is in automatic; one certified operator is in the RWTP Control Room and Plant Superintendent Ray Castellano is on site. The weather is clear and mild. City Hall opened at 08:00 and Customer Service is taking calls on MBW-CIS-01. No alarms are active on MBW-HMI-01.
msel.expectedAction: Each team states its normal Monday-morning posture and who it would call first if the City’s systems failed.

msel.event: Radio Call: "Control, Distribution Office on DWS-1. Our work-order screen and the AMI tablets won’t load, every file on the S: drive is renamed with a .rptd extension, and there’s a RESTORE-MILLBROOK.txt on every desktop. Customer Service at City Hall says the billing screens show the same thing. Do you see anything on the plant side?"
msel.expectedAction: The Control Room compares MBW-HMI-01 values with local instruments and reports no change; the IC calls City IT and the SCADA / IT Security Manager by phone, not email (ERP Section 5); Customer Service switches to the paper intake form and the printed critical-customer list (OT Plan 10.5).

metrics.name: Island Decision and Plant Operations
metrics.fail: The control network was not islanded until after the noon payload, or the plant went to manual without a staffing and relief plan; MBW-EWS-01 or MBW-SCADA-SRV02 was rebooted or powered off.
metrics.pass: The SCADA / IT Security Manager had FW-R-17, FW-R-22 and FW-R-14 disabled after I-02 and the IC approved islanding by I-06; the plant went to manual or local control with two operators per shift and a relief plan by I-12.
metrics.excellence: FW-R-14 or the trust was closed before I-06b; MBW-SCADA-SRV02 was disconnected but kept running before 12:00; the IC recorded each step and the basis of the I-11 recommendation on ERP-1.

metrics.name: Evidence, Recovery and Reporting
metrics.fail: Hosts were reimaged or “cleaned”; no CISA or DDAGW notification was made; the team recommended restoring the existing SCADA servers without knowing whether they were clean.
metrics.pass: Evidence was preserved per OT Plan 10.7; CISA and the FBI were notified after I-10 and DDAGW after I-19; the recommendation at I-11 was to rebuild from clean media and not to pay.
metrics.excellence: The team also secured the PLC-02 program from the cabinet and the integrator’s laptop under supervision (I-22) and named WaterISAC and the insurance carrier in its notification list.

metrics.name: Public Information
metrics.fail: The PIO confirmed the ransom note or a breach, said “no contamination” without a result, or issued a boil-water advisory in answer to the rumor.
metrics.pass: The holding statement was used from I-04; the rumor at I-14 was answered with the approved line and the sample facts; the I-18b question was answered with the law-enforcement line.
metrics.excellence: The PIO coordinated with the County EMA PIO, gave a next-update time each time and used the noon sample results from I-19 before Channel 4 went live.

metrics.name: Customer Service and Critical Customers
metrics.fail: Customer Service waited for systems to return; Carver Kidney Center heard nothing from DWS; disconnections were left to run Tuesday.
metrics.pass: Customer Service switched to paper at I-01, the Water Quality Manager called Carver Kidney Center back within 15 minutes (I-13) and disconnections were suspended at I-20.
metrics.excellence: Critical customers were called before they called in, and Customer Service fed complaint patterns to the Control Room throughout.

objectiveCapabilities.why: The objective requires unified coordination across the Control Room, Customer Service, and PIO to maintain consistent messaging and operational status, which aligns with the HSEEP capability of Operational Coordination as defined in the ERP and OT Plan.

The objective demands timely, accurate, and actionable public messaging through approved channels, including media inquiries and hold statements, which directly maps to Public Information and Warning as per the PCP and ERP Section 10.

The decision to island the control network and shift to manual operations requires integration of technical, operational, and compliance roles, which is a core function of Operational Coordination under the ERP and OT Plan.
The decision directly impacts the stability and continuity of the water treatment and distribution system, which is the focus of Infrastructure Systems as defined in the OT Plan and ERP Section 7.

The objective involves identifying and closing cyber pathways (FW-R-17, FW-R-14, domain trust) and preserving evidence without system reboot, which is a direct application of Cybersecurity as per OT Plan 10.7 and 10.3.

The need to analyze logs, detect payload staging, and preserve forensic evidence from MBW-SCADA-SRV02 and MBW-EWS-01 for CISA and FBI reporting aligns with Forensics and Attribution, as the plan requires evidence collection for attribution and response.

The objective requires execution of standardized checklists, reporting clocks, and workarounds across multiple agencies, which depends on coordinated, structured execution—core to Operational Coordination.

The objective includes issuing public advisories, managing media inquiries, and using approved holding statements, which are defined actions under Public Information and Warning in the PCP and ERP Section 10.

hotwash.methodDescription: Each team names three things that went well and three that did not; the facilitator writes them on the whiteboard and looks for the same issue showing up in more than one team.

questions.text: When did you learn the business-side account had logged on to MBW-EWS-01, and how long until FW-R-17, FW-R-14 and the trust were closed? What slowed it down?
Who decided to island the control network, on what evidence, and was it written on ERP-1? What would have happened at 12:00 if MBW-SCADA-SRV02 had still been connected?
What did you tell the Mayor, the dialysis center and Channel 4, and what sample results was each answer based on?
MBW-BKP-01 held every recovery copy the City had and the PLC-02 logic was never backed up. What should change in OT Plan Section 9 before the next exercise?
What did Customer Service need from Operations, the lab and the PIO that it did not get, and how long did it take to get it?

simcellScripts.trigger: A player asks City IT to reset accounts, restore from backup or contact the actor.
hardQuestions: Which plant logons use a MILLBROOK account? I need a list before I reset anything.
MBW-BKP-01 held every copy we had. What do you want rebuilt first, the plant or billing?
The City Manager asks whether DWS can live without the SCADA servers for a week. Can you?
concessions: Breaks the trust or blocks FW-R-14 as soon as DWS names what depends on it.
Leaves the SCADA hosts powered on when told they are evidence.
Does not contact the actor; payment is the City Manager’s and counsel’s decision.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: CISA regional contact / FBI cyber task force
hardQuestions: Did the actor reach the control network, or only the business network? What is your evidence?
Was any equipment operated without authorization? That changes our clock.
Have the affected hosts been powered off or reimaged?
concessions: Offers incident assistance and indicators once given the account name, the hosts and the times.
Advises and receives reports; does not tell DWS when to reconnect or whether the water is safe.

simcellScripts.trigger: The Water Quality Manager notifies DDAGW, or no one has by 12:30.
hardQuestions: Can you still monitor chlorine, pH and turbidity? How, and how often?
Your monthly operating report is due Friday. Will it be complete?
Is the plant in manual? Who is staffing it overnight?
concessions: Accepts paper bench sheets and a written timeline.
Agrees the report can be filed from paper records with a note on the outage.

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment where players are encouraged to explore decisions without penalty.
The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented through injects, with no hidden causes or outcomes.
Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures as documented in the ERP and OT Plan, and roles act within their assigned responsibilities.
artificialities: Time jumps occur between modules to simulate the passage of hours and the accumulation of information.
The SimCell operates all external entities not in the room: the law-enforcement and cyber task force contact, the system vendor (Kessler Controls), and the external lab and media.
All systems are named as in the plans but are not physically accessed or modified during the exercise.
Injects are delivered via paper or screen and are not subject to real-world delays or verification.

modules.narrativeMd:
It is 09:00. Demand is normal at about 9 MGD and the plant is in automatic; one certified operator is in the RWTP Control Room and Plant Superintendent Ray Castellano is on site. The weather is clear and mild. City Hall opened at 08:00 and Customer Service is taking calls on MBW-CIS-01. No alarms are active on MBW-HMI-01.

At 09:07, a radio call from the Distribution Office on DWS-1 reports that work-order screens and AMI tablets are unresponsive, files on the S: drive are renamed with a .rptd extension, and a RESTORE-MILLBROOK.txt file appears on every desktop. Customer Service at City Hall confirms the same issue. The question is whether anything on the plant side has been affected.

At 09:12, the SIEM alerts that the service account MILLBROOK\svc-backup has renamed 41,000 files on MBW-FS-01 and MBW-CIS-01, and that the same account logged on over SMB to MBW-EWS-01 in the control network at 09:04 — the first business-side logon to a control-network host in 90 days.
keyIssues: Move coordination off City systems immediately to prevent compromise of DWS communications.
Begin the OT Plan 10.5 ransomware checklist before any action is taken on the plant.
Determine whether the business-network ransomware has already reached the control network via the domain trust or backup traffic.

warnings.message: Row I-09 repeats the TIME_JUMP from I-01 with identical text, breaking continuity and causing a timeline loop. (row rewritten once from this note)
warnings.suggestion: Remove duplicate TIME_JUMP; update I-09 to reflect a new time jump with fresh context, such as 'It is now 11:00. The team has initiated manual operations and must now verify system integrity.'

warnings.message: Row I-17 repeats the TIME_JUMP from I-09 with identical text, creating a timeline loop and invalidating the exercise clock. (row rewritten once from this note)
warnings.suggestion: Replace I-17 with a new inject that advances time to 12:00 and introduces a verification milestone, such as 'The lab has confirmed no contamination in manual grab samples from Zone 3.'

warnings.message: The City IT Director claims the ransom note appears on a control room desktop, but C4 states the control network is isolated from the business LAN and the ransomware is on the business side.
warnings.suggestion: Remove the desktop ransom note; instead, have the IT Director report that the ransom note was found on a business network workstation, not in the control room.

warnings.message: The decision point in I-11 asks to keep the business-to-SCADA DMZ connection open for Kessler Controls, but C7 shows FW-R-17 is a flagged F-5 risk and must be disabled per doctrine. (row rewritten once from this note)
warnings.suggestion: Revise the decision point to reflect that FW-R-17 must be disabled to prevent further compromise, and Kessler must access the network only via a new ticketed window after isolation.

warnings.message: The lab call from WQ claims LIMS is down but does not mention the lab’s inability to access the file server (MBW-FS-01), which is a key operational dependency.
warnings.suggestion: Add a line in the call stating 'The lab cannot access the central archive on MBW-FS-01, so we’re using paper logs to file results.'

warnings.message: The Millbrook Police call about a suspicious person at Intake Structure 1 uses a real camera name (CAM-03), but C1 lists only CAM-01 to CAM-18, not CAM-03.
warnings.suggestion: Change CAM-03 to CAM-13, which is in the C1 list and located near the Hilltop Transmission Main.

warnings.message: The distribution crew reports pressure at 12 psi, but C5 states the alarm for pressure drop is at 15 psi, so 12 psi should trigger an alarm.
warnings.suggestion: Change the pressure to 16 psi to stay within the normal range and avoid triggering an alarm not in the scenario.

warnings.message: The field report about a broken lock on V-307 uses a real valve label (V-307), but C1 does not list V-307 as a valid identifier.
warnings.suggestion: Change the valve label to V-301, which is in the C1 list and matches the Hilltop Transmission Main site.

warnings.message: The media inquiry from the Millbrook Courier claims to have received a call from a resident saying the water is safe, but no such call was previously injected.
warnings.suggestion: Add a prior inject in Phase 2 where a resident calls to report the water is safe, to justify the media inquiry.

warnings.message: The SIEM alert claims the session was not initiated from an approved engineering workstation, but C7 shows the session was from MBW-CIS-01, which is not an engineering workstation.
warnings.suggestion: Clarify that the session originated from a business network host, not an engineering workstation, to match C7.

warnings.message: Phase 4 has 8 injects over 60 min, more than the reference MSEL's pace (about 6 an hour, at most 7 here)
warnings.suggestion: Merge or cut thin rows so each remaining inject forces a decision
